theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixMuon_equipartition
theorems.informal: If O Oᵀ = 1 then tr((E O)ᵀ (E O)) = tr(Eᵀ E) for every matrix E (any number of rows); frob form: matrixMuon_frob_mul_orth.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixMuon_energy_proj
theorems.informal: For an orthogonal projector E and O Oᵀ = 1: ‖E O‖_F² = tr E.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixMuon_energy_proj_rank
theorems.informal: Same with tr E replaced by rank E (uses MatrixMuon.IsOrthProj.trace_eq_rank: trace of an idempotent real matrix is its rank).

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixMuon_energy_total
theorems.informal: ‖O‖_F² = d = |ι| when O Oᵀ = 1.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixMuon_energy_fraction
theorems.informal: Fraction of the Muon update energy in the range of an orthogonal projector is tr E / d, irrespective of the gradient (d > 0 assumed); coordinate-block version matrixMuon_energy_fraction_coordProj gives |T|/d.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixMuon_sgd_energy_fraction
theorems.paperItem: filter_spec 5.1 (remark 'for SGD that fraction equals θ')
theorems.informal: In the coordinate model A = diag(P.lam), W = diag(c) Q: ‖Π_D G‖_F²/‖G‖_F² = P.theta c for the clean gradient G = A W (via matrixMuon_grad_energy_coordProj = P.mom T 2 c and matrixMuon_grad_energy = P.s c).

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixMuon_muon_energy_fraction
theorems.informal: For P : Spec ι and any O with O Oᵀ = 1: ‖Π_D O‖_F²/‖O‖_F² = P.kR / d.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixMuon_loss_step
theorems.informal: For symmetric A: L(W − ηD) = L(W) − η⟪AW, D⟫ + (η²/2) tr(Dᵀ A D) for every direction D.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixMuon_loss_projected_step
theorems.informal: A symmetric, E orthogonal projector, any O with O Oᵀ = 1: L(W − ηEO) − L(W) = −η⟪EAW, O⟫ + (η²/2) tr(EA). No commutation of E with A and no PSD of A needed.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixMuon_loss_projected_step_noisy
theorems.informal: Same identity when O is the polar factor of an arbitrary (noisy) gradient G.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixMuon_loss_full_step
theorems.informal: L(W − ηO) − L(W) = −η⟪AW, O⟫ + (η²/2) tr A.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixMuon_loss_projected_step_needs_symm
theorems.informal: Formal counterexample (d = n = 2): for non-symmetric A the 5.2 identity fails (0 ≠ −1).

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixMuon_proj_grad_of_commute
theorems.informal: If E A = A E then E A W = A (E W).

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixMuon_frob_proj_grad
theorems.informal: If (S, O) is a left polar pair of A W then ⟪E A W, O⟫ = tr(E S) for every square E (general form matrixMuon_frob_mul_mul_orth needs only O Oᵀ = 1).

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixMuon_frob_grad_polar
theorems.informal: For a left polar pair of G: ⟪G, O⟫ = tr S.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixMuon_frob_grad_polar_eq_nuclear
theorems.informal: ⟪G, O⟫ = Σ_i √(eigenvalue_i(G Gᵀ)), the sum of singular values (Mathlib has no nuclear norm); also matrixMuon_frob_grad_polar_pos: ⟪G, O⟫ > 0 if G ≠ 0.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixMuon_loss_projected_step_noiseFree
theorems.informal: Noise-free: L(W − ηEO) − L(W) = −η tr(ES) + (η²/2) tr(EA).

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixMuon_loss_decrease_iff
theorems.informal: A symmetric, E orthogonal projector, (S,O) left polar pair of A W, tr(EA) > 0: loss decreases iff 0 < η < 2 tr(ES)/tr(EA), for all real η (spec's tr(ES) > 0 not needed).

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixMuon_loss_increase_iff
theorems.informal: Same hypotheses: loss increases iff η < 0 or η > 2 tr(ES)/tr(EA); matrixMuon_loss_eq_iff: unchanged iff η = 0 or η = threshold; matrixMuon_threshold_pos: threshold > 0 when both traces are.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixMuon_traces_pos
theorems.informal: If A and (AW)(AW)ᵀ are positive definite, then tr(EA) > 0 and tr(ES) > 0 for every nonzero orthogonal projector E.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixMuon_isLeftPolar_sqrt
theorems.informal: If G Gᵀ is positive definite then (CFC.sqrt (G Gᵀ), (CFC.sqrt (G Gᵀ))⁻¹ G) is a left polar pair of G; matrixMuon_exists_leftPolar is the ∃ form.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixMuon_leftPolar_unique
theorems.informal: If G Gᵀ is positive definite, two left polar pairs of G coincide; matrixMuon_existsUnique_leftPolar (∃!) and matrixMuon_isLeftPolar_iff (characterisation S = √(GGᵀ), O = S⁻¹G).

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.MatrixMuon.IsLeftPolar.eq_sqrt
theorems.informal: In any left polar pair S = (G Gᵀ)^{1/2} (no rank assumption); IsLeftPolar.mul_self: S² = G Gᵀ.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.MatrixMuon.IsLeftPolar.card_le
theorems.informal: A left polar pair forces |ι| ≤ |κ|; matrixMuon_card_le_of_posDef and matrixMuon_posDef_iff_isUnit_det (G Gᵀ PD iff invertible).

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixMuon_leftPolar_not_unique
theorems.informal: G = 0 (d = n = 1) has the two left polar pairs (0, 1) and (0, −1).

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixMuon_isLeftPolar_diagonal
theorems.informal: σ_i ≥ 0, Q Qᵀ = 1 ⇒ (diag σ, Q) is a left polar pair of diag(σ) Q; matrixMuon_leftPolar_diagonal_unique: for σ_i > 0 it is the only one.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixMuon_trace_ratio_coordProj
theorems.informal: tr(Π_T diag σ)/tr(Π_T diag λ) = Σ_{i∈T} σ_i / Σ_{i∈T} λ_i for the coordinate projector on a finset T.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixMuon_step_row
theorems.informal: G = diag(σ) Q, σ_i > 0, any left polar pair (S,O): row i of diag(r) Q − ηO is (r_i − η)·Q_i.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixMuon_coordinate_step
theorems.informal: A = diag(λ), λ_i > 0, W = diag(c) Q, c_i ≠ 0: for every left polar pair of A W, W − ηO = diag(c_i − η sign c_i) Q (row form matrixMuon_coordinate_step_row; explicit polar pair matrixMuon_isLeftPolar_coordinate).

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixMuon_coordinate_loss_decrease_iff
theorems.informal: P : Spec ι, W = diag(c) Q, c_i ≠ 0, T nonempty: projected Muon step decreases the matrix loss iff 0 < η < 2 Σ_T λ_i|c_i| / Σ_T λ_i; with matrixMuon_loss_eq_specLoss (matrix loss = P.loss c) and matrixMuon_coordinate_projected_step.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixFilter_id / matrixFilter_one
theorems.paperItem: filter_spec header (SGD f = id, Muon f = 1)
theorems.informal: With filterDir f S O := cfc f S * O: f = id gives G, f ≡ 1 gives O.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixFilter_svd
theorems.paperItem: filter_spec header F(G) = U f(Σ) Vᵀ
theorems.informal: For a thin SVD G = U diag(σ) V (U orthogonal, σ ≥ 0, V Vᵀ = 1): (U diag σ Uᵀ, U V) is a left polar pair and f(S) O = U diag(f σ) V; matrixFilter_svd_unique: for σ > 0 this holds for every left polar pair.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixFilter_diagonal
theorems.informal: G = diag(σ) Q, σ_i > 0: for every left polar pair, f(S) O = diag(f σ_i) Q (uses MatrixMuon.cfc_diagonal, proved here).

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixFilter_step_row
theorems.informal: A = diag(λ), W = diag(r) Q, λ_i, r_i > 0: row i of W − η f(S) O is (r_i − η f(λ_i r_i))·Q_i.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.matrixFilter_coordinate_step
theorems.informal: Signed commuting state: W − η f(S) O = diag(c_i − η sign(λ_i c_i) f(|λ_i c_i|)) Q; Spec version matrixFilter_spec_step; basis-free version matrixFilter_coordinate_step_basis (A = U diag(λ) Uᵀ, W = U diag(c) Q) with matrixMuon_loss_conj.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.MatrixMuon.Example.ex_loss_decrease_iff
theorems.informal: d = 2, n = 3, A = diag(3,1), S = [[2,1],[1,2]] not commuting with A, explicit O, W: left polar pair (ex_isLeftPolar), G Gᵀ PD and pair unique (ex_posDef, ex_unique), loss decreases iff 0 < η < 4/3, energy fraction 1/2.

paperIssues: Spec 5.2: the hypothesis 'Π commutes with A' is superfluous. tr((ΠO)ᵀA(ΠO)) = tr(ΠAΠ) = tr(Π²A) = tr(ΠA) by cyclicity of the trace, and the first-order term only uses Πᵀ = Π. Proved without it (matrixMuon_loss_projected_step); confirmed numerically with random non-commuting projectors. Commutation only matters for the interpretation ΠAW = A(ΠW) (matrixMuon_proj_grad_of_commute).

Spec 5.2: positive semidefiniteness of A is not needed; symmetry of A is needed. Formal counterexample for non-symmetric A: A = [[0,1],[0,0]], W = [[0,-1],[1,0]], Π = O = 1, η = 1 gives left side 0, right side -1 (matrixMuon_loss_projected_step_needs_symm).
Spec 5.3: ⟪ΠAW, O⟫ = tr(ΠS) holds for arbitrary square Π and S once AW = SO and OOᵀ = 1 (no projector/symmetry/PSD needed).

Spec 5.3: the hypothesis tr(ΠS) > 0 is not needed for the iff. With tr(ΠA) > 0 alone, loss decreases iff 0 < η < 2tr(ΠS)/tr(ΠA) for all real η, because tr(ΠS) ≥ 0 is automatic for an orthogonal projector and PSD S; tr(ΠS) > 0 only makes the interval nonempty.

Spec 5.4: uniqueness of S never needs definiteness (S = (GGᵀ)^{1/2} always); only uniqueness of O does, and it genuinely fails otherwise: G = 0 with d = n = 1 has polar pairs (0,1) and (0,-1) (matrixMuon_leftPolar_not_unique).
Spec 5.5: (diag σ, Q) is a left polar pair already for σ_i ≥ 0; σ_i > 0 is what makes it the unique one.

Spec 5.1/5.3 wording: 'rank k' and 'nuclear norm' are identified with tr Π and tr S without proof; both identifications are proved here (trace of an idempotent = rank; tr S = Σ √eigenvalues(GGᵀ)). Mathlib has no nuclear norm, so it is expressed through eigenvalues of GGᵀ.
Lean technicality: Π is a reserved token, so the projector is named E throughout. No claim of spec §5 was found to be false.
